title: Evaluation of secondary suturing as a treatment option for infection-free port wound dehiscence
summary:
A port system is used for patients with chronic diseases who require long-term intravenous therapy. It is used for chemotherapy, parenteral nutrition and hemodialysis, among other things. To implant a port system, the jugular vein is first punctured with ultrasound, then a wire and the port catheter are inserted into the superior vena cava. A small space is then prepared in the area of the chest wall in which the port chamber is placed. The port catheter is inserted under the skin and connected to the chamber.
A port infection is the most common and potentially life-threatening complication following this treatment. A rare but equally problematic complication is port wound dehiscence, in which the wound around the port chamber in the chest area breaks open. However, this complication has not yet been sufficiently investigated. Initial small studies have shown that infection-free port wound dehiscence occurs more frequently in patients who are treated with certain drugs such as bevacizumab. It also showed that children have fewer problems with wound opening when the sutures are continuous compared to single-button sutures. Due to the incomplete study situation, there is still no standardized procedure for the treatment of such wounds without infection. In such cases, some clinics opt for secondary suturing, i.e. re-suturing the port wound dehiscence, while other centers remove the entire port system to avoid the risk of infection.
This raises the question of how patients with an infection-free port wound dehiscence should best be treated, taking into account the risk of infection and the need for reimplantation of the port. The aim of this study is to retrospectively collect missing data from several clinics in order to find answers for the optimal patient management of this complication. All patients who have had a port wound dehiscence in the last ten years will be included in this study.  The study will not only examine how the medical treatment of port wound dehiscence was carried out, but also the results and possible complications. In addition, factors that may influence the occurrence of such port wound dehiscence will be investigated.
conditions: Follow-up examination after unspecified treatment for malignant neoplasm

interventions.name: All patients who had a port implantation in the interventional radiology department of one of the participating centers in the period August 2014 - August 2024 and did not have a port infection after the primary suture

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Port implantation in interventional radiology during the study period
Exclusion criteria:
Port infection after primary suture
